A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProtoMech research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein-family classification, function prediction, circuit discovery, steering experiments, and biological case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds ESM2-35M experiments, windowed-CLT evaluation, circuit-stability analyses, and additional steering comparisons.

M1.justification: v2 introduces windowed CLTs, restricting each decoder to a width-w layer window instead of all preceding layers (Appendix G.3, Equation 14). This changes cross-layer connectivity and computational requirements; a width-four variant is trained and evaluated. The original circuit-discovery and steering procedures remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use UniRef50 training sequences, Swiss-Prot/InterPro family tasks, the same 12 ProteinGym assays, and the same seven steering assays. The new mutation-depth and stability analyses reuse existing coverage; larger backbones change model configurations rather than datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained PLT, CAA, and random-mutation comparisons, v2 evaluates ESM2-logit mutation selection on seven steering assays (Table 8) and PEX and GGS on the GB1 and HIS7 assays (Table 9). These substantially broaden the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds ESM2-35M configurations and evaluation protocols, including 1,024-example test subsamples for four assays and 128-example, fitness-balanced validation samples for multiple-mutant circuit discovery. It also specifies ten-round PEX/GGS comparisons and mutation-depth and circuit-overlap evaluations. Appendix A revises the reported auxiliary-loss setting from k_aux=floor(d_ESM/2) to 32, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds GFP prediction analysis stratified by mutation depth, circuit-node overlap across family inputs and training folds, and a windowed-versus-standard CLT accuracy/cost comparison. These test functional consistency, circuit stability, and connectivity tradeoffs beyond v1's retained replacement-model ablations and biological case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 newly specifies that the mutation-depth analysis uses the circuit discovered with the first random seed. Existing cross-validation, steering-trial counts, and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained; the revision does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for ESM2-35M, windowed CLTs, mutation-depth retention, circuit overlap, and new steering comparators. For example, sequential 35M circuits achieve family F1 of 0.80 ± 0.12 and function Spearman correlation of 0.38 ± 0.19 (Appendix G). The original five tables and Figures 1–8 retain their results, while Section 3.1 changes the stated 8M function-circuit recovery from 74% to 76% without changing its reported correlation.

T1.justification: Appendix F.1 corrects the edge-weight formula to use the target latent's encoder rather than the source latent's encoder. Equation 14 additionally defines the restricted decoder summation for windowed CLTs. These are localized mathematical changes; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about computational replacement, compact circuits, steering, and biological interpretability. The additional experiments support these claims without rewriting their headline scope.

C2.justification: v1 presents larger-model scaling as future work; v2 interprets 35M and windowed-CLT results as evidence of improved feasibility and an accuracy/compute tradeoff. It also adds global-functional-rule and circuit-stability interpretations, and explicitly identifies autoregressive and diffusion-model extensions as unresolved applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 documents 35M latent dimensions and sparsity, newly discloses explicit LayerNorm in the 8M implementation and its omission for 35M, and supplies window width and additional evaluation settings. Appendix G.3 and Table 10 add NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware information, parameter counts, and training-time estimates, including extrapolations for larger models. Code and visualizer access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ren et al. (2022) and Kirjner et al. (2024) for PEX/GGS comparisons, and Shu et al. (2026) as inspiration for windowed CLTs. These extend positioning toward protein optimization and scalable circuit tracing while retaining the existing SAE/transcoder framing.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 adds focused discussion subsections and a scaling appendix, moves the SAE comparison from Appendix G to H, clarifies terminology, and updates the publication header and acknowledgments. This is a localized expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds mutation-depth Tables 3–4, comparator Tables 8–9, resource Table 10, and scaling/windowed-model Figures 15–16. Existing steering tables are renumbered, the SAE schematic becomes Figure 17, and appendix displays are redistributed and resized. The substantial change is new visual evidence, while Figures 1–8 and the interface screenshots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's untested scalability limitation through actual ESM2-35M experiments and an evaluated windowed architecture that reduces parameters from 207M to 125M while retaining 82% versus 85% family-task performance. Broader comparators and circuit-stability checks strengthen validation. The gains remain substantial despite limitations: mutation-depth evidence uses one seed, larger-model timings are extrapolated, and Appendix G's latent-space percentages are inconsistent with its stated 12 × 4800 latent space.
